title: Formally Verifying Analog Neural Networks with Device Mismatch Variations
problem: Analog neural networks suffer from inherent circuit deviations and must be extensively tested for correct behavior under device mismatch variations. Monte Carlo simulation-based verification is prohibitively time- and resource-intensive.
motivation: Analog circuits provide energy- and area-efficient implementations of neural networks, but their sensitivity to device variations requires robust verification before deployment.
method: Rather than testing analog neural networks through thousands of simulations with random variations (called Monte Carlo simulation), this work uses formal verification—a mathematical approach that proves correctness by analyzing all possible behaviors at once. The key technique is reachability analysis, which calculates what outputs an analog circuit can produce when its components deviate from ideal values (device mismatch). By mathematically proving the circuit produces correct outputs even under worst-case deviations, the approach avoids the time and computing resources that exhaustive simulation requires.
key_novelty: Formal verification with reachability analysis can mathematically prove analog neural networks produce correct outputs even when components vary, eliminating the need for extensive simulations.
contributions: Reduce test time from days to milliseconds using reachability analysis
Faster and more scalable solution for analog neural circuit verification
Modeling methodology for device mismatch variations in formal context
